_meta.description: Flag register. Status: open | resolved | standing. Open flags are published on the Flagged for Review page and do not block publication. Every flag carries an evidence link. IDs F-01…F-67 are carried from the prior project registers (S-PRIOR3, S-PRIOR4) with their evidence; F-Pxx are new in this project.
_meta.last_change: 2026-11-20 (arena/0a9f19fe-prod2): F-P29 added and marked resolved - the conflict-marker / unclosed-block stylesheet defect and the new browser-free stylesheet gate. | 2026-11-20 (arena/e1dbef32-prod2, union merge): this pass's rows land at F-P35, F-P33, F-P31, F-P32, F-P34, F-P30 after main's highest row, so both sets are kept and no id was reused. Remap of this session's own earlier numbers: F-P25..F-P30, Q-P18..Q-P21, SG-48..SG-54, D-P23..D-P26. | 2026-11-20 (arena/e1dbef32-prod2, integration): F-P36..F-P39 appended — three defects that shipped on main's merged tip (FAQ markup that did not match its page, two gate failures main passed through, a gate section that parsed nothing because of a query string) and one documentation count that lagged the code. All four are fixed on this branch and each carries a reproduction command. Append-only; no earlier row edited.

flags.title: Product-level commission rate is unverified
flags.detail: The official Standard Commission Income Statement Table 1 lists Kitchen at 4.50% and Home at 3.00%. No official source reviewed maps these ASINs to a commission category, so every product-level rate is published blank. Do not infer a rate from the category band.
flags.how_to_resolve: Read the product-level rate from an Associates Central report after enrollment (owner action).

flags.title: Prices and star ratings are not published
flags.detail: Prices, ratings and review counts change constantly and would need a dated-snapshot discipline this site has not adopted (see D-19 for the evidence rule). They are visible on every listing and were observed during verification, but are withheld from all published pages. The site compares formats and listed specifications instead.
flags.evidence_note: S-P1; standing editorial rule carried from the prior register
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner decision: adopt a dated-snapshot price policy (queued as suggestion SG-05) or keep the rule.

flags.title: Supplied short links carry no tag= parameter
flags.detail: Every observed redirect of the five owner-supplied short links shows Amazon source-token parameters but no tag= parameter. Without an enrolled tag the clicks cannot be attributed. The site therefore publishes tagged Special Links built from the verified ASINs (D-01/D-14), and claims no attributed click or order.
flags.evidence_note: S-POL; observations in data/p2/verification-2026-11-19.json
flags.how_to_resolve: Run the one-link-per-product test in Associates Central (F-58).

flags.title: P3 belongs to a 6/8/9-quart size-variant family
flags.detail: Four GTINs are listed on the B08DKYBTPH page, confirming a size-variant family. A buyer (or a cart) can end up with a different size than the 8 qt record published here.
flags.evidence_note: S-P3, Item details read 2026-11-14
flags.how_to_resolve: None needed for publication; buyers are warned on the product row.

flags.title: Popularity and 'trending' claims need dated snapshots
flags.detail: Per decision D-19, a popularity claim is allowed only as a dated snapshot of an official page (page + read date named in the copy). Bare adjectives like 'trending' or 'best-selling' are banned from the copy rules.
flags.evidence_note: S-GHELP; rule adopted 2026-11-16 (carried)
flags.how_to_resolve: Standing rule; enforced by tools/checks.py word blacklist.

flags.title: Analytics endpoint is deployable but not yet hosted
flags.detail: GitHub Pages is static hosting. The privacy-preserving counter (docs/assets/js/measure.js) and the self-hosted endpoint (server.mjs, POST /api/events, Node 20+, no dependencies) ship with the site, but no server is deployed and settings.analytics_endpoint is empty, so the site sends nothing anywhere. Browser-local counts are visible to each visitor only and are not shared data. This flag previously cited a path, analytics-endpoint/server.py, that was never committed — corrected 2026-11-20 (F-P22).
flags.evidence_note: server.mjs at the repo root; ANALYTICS-ENDPOINT.md documents it; tests/server.test.mjs covers it (npm test). Corrected 2026-11-20.
flags.how_to_resolve: Host server.mjs somewhere owner-controlled (behind HTTPS), set settings.analytics_endpoint, rebuild. Resolve F-P23 first: the endpoint's event vocabulary does not currently match the site's five events.

flags.title: P2's listing states its cooking-function count in two ways
flags.detail: Listing sections have described the B09B7SB46R as having 24 cooking functions / 24 one-touch presets, while another count of 25 appeared in prior reads of a different section. The site publishes '24 as listed' with the read date and never a synthesized number.
flags.how_to_resolve: Count the presets on the listing during a dated re-read (any session).

flags.title: 'Also viewed' carousels change between reads
flags.detail: Carousel membership and order on the three air-fryer listings changed again on the 2026-11-19 read (P1 slots 2/3 swapped vs 2026-11-14; P3 slot 2 replaced). Carousel data is stored as dated observations only and is never presented as a stable 'competitor set'.
flags.evidence_note: S-P1; observations in data/p2/verification-2026-11-19.json
flags.how_to_resolve: Standing volatility; re-read on each verification pass.

flags.title: P2's listing title second segment drifts between reads
flags.detail: The B09B7SB46R listing title's second segment changed across the 2026-11-14, 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-19 reads. The site publishes the current string with its read date and keeps previous strings in the register (see also F-66).
flags.evidence_note: S-P2; strings recorded in data/p2/verification-2026-11-19.json and data/p2/products.json
flags.how_to_resolve: Standing volatility; the register keeps the dated history.

flags.title: Default offers can be used items (Amazon Resale)
flags.detail: On the 2026-11-16 reads the default offers on B0CDY277D3 and B08DKYBTPH were used items sold by Amazon Resale. Buyers should check the seller and condition on the listing. Not re-observed on the 2026-11-19 read.
flags.evidence_note: S-P1; prior read 2026-11-16 (S-PRIOR4)
flags.how_to_resolve: Standing buyer warning.

flags.title: Two newly submitted short links were unverified — resolved 2026-11-19
flags.detail: The brief's two additional links (link.amazon/B0c8moW59, link.amazon/B0f3GKalj) were unresolved at the time of the prior register (they were excluded from product pages then — that exclusion did not mean either was invalid). The 2026-11-19 session resolved both: B0DHZTCNR5 (ThermoMaven 1-sec thermometer) and B0DZFD6R9Z (CHEF iQ Sense Gen3), read their official listings, and added them to the register as P4/P5. Product-intent records for all five links remain separate from observed redirects.
flags.evidence_note: S-P4, S-P5; data/p2/verification-2026-11-19.json
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved 2026-11-19. Attribution of these links remains governed by F-57/F-58.

flags.title: Tracking ID registration is confirmable only inside Associates Central
flags.detail: The owner supplied shopnow047c-20 and its format matches the documented US Store ID pattern (ends in -20). Whether it is registered, active, and belongs to an enrolled account cannot be confirmed from outside Associates Central. Until then the site publishes the links but claims no attributed click, order or revenue.
flags.evidence_note: S-TAG, read 2026-11-17
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner logs into Associates Central and confirms the Partner Tag (Q-01).

flags.title: One-link-per-product Associates test not yet run
flags.detail: The enrolled-workflow test (generate/validate one Special Link per product, confirm destination and a test click in the reporting) gates attribution claims and scaling — not publication. It cannot run from a build sandbox.
flags.evidence_note: S-POL
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner runs the test per the protocol on the measurement page.

flags.title: P2 title-segment drift (prior-register instance)
flags.detail: Prior instance of F-44: the stored second title segment dated 2026-11-14 differed from the 2026-11-15 read. Carried for history; the 2026-11-19 read extended the drift record again.
flags.evidence_note: S-P2; S-PRIOR4
flags.how_to_resolve: Merged into F-44 going forward; kept for the dated trail.

flags.title: Short-link path codes are not ASINs
flags.detail: Amazon defines an ASIN as a 10-character alphanumeric identifier appearing after /dp/ in the product URL (S-ASIN). The submitted path codes (e.g. B04G1MEwY) are nine characters and live in the short-link path. They are recorded as link_path_code only and are never used as ASINs.
flags.evidence_note: S-ASIN, read 2026-11-17
flags.how_to_resolve: Standing rule.

flags.title: P4's page shows two different waterproofing subtitle strings
flags.detail: The B0DHZTCNR5 page <title> says 'IP67 Waterproof for Grill BBQ' while the Product Summary heading on the same page says 'Highly Waterproof for Grill BBQ Camping'. Both are recorded verbatim; published copy uses the <title> string with its 2026-11-19 read date and states IP67 only as 'listed in the title'.
flags.how_to_resolve: Confirm the certified IP rating from the manufacturer's documentation if it becomes available (owner).

flags.title: Product scope: thermometers joined an air-fryer catalog — resolved 2026-11-19
flags.detail: The owner's brief lists five products to market; three resolve to air fryers and two (resolved 2026-11-19) to meat thermometers. The publication organizes them by format under one kitchen theme (countertop cooking + doneness tools) per decision D-P01. Not an irregularity in the data — recorded so the scope change is visible.
flags.evidence_note: S-P5; decision D-P01
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved by D-P01 (2026-11-19).

flags.title: P1 capacity unit wording differs between title and spec table
flags.detail: The B0CDY277D3 title states 6 Quart (2 × 3Qt baskets); the spec table read 2026-11-14 states '6 liters'. 6 qt is about 5.7 L, so the two wordings are not equal. Published copy uses the title wording with its read date; both readings are recorded.
flags.evidence_note: S-P1; title read 2026-11-19, spec table read 2026-11-14
flags.how_to_resolve: Re-read the spec table in a dated session and record whichever the listing shows.

flags.title: P5 is a size-variant listing (1/2/3/4 probes)
flags.detail: The B0DZFD6R9Z listing offers 1/2/3/4-probe configurations. This record is the 3-probe Gen3 configuration shown in the title. Buyers should confirm the probe count in the variant selector.
flags.how_to_resolve: Standing buyer warning.

flags.title: Two registers disagree on whether prices are published
flags.detail: data/products.json (the earlier Countercraft build) carries buy-box prices for all five ASINs (as listed on 2026-11-19; values are kept in that file only). data/p2/ withholds prices and ratings entirely (F-02). The earlier build's executive-summary appendix therefore conflicts with this build's rule. The Prod2 site publishes no prices.
flags.evidence_note: Price text as observed on the official listing, read 2026-11-19 (arena/236bc1ed-prod2 recheck).
flags.how_to_resolve: Decision under Q-27 / SG-05. Until a dated-snapshot rule is adopted and automated, prices stay unpublished here. The Countercraft build stays archived and is not mirrored.

flags.title: Short-link redirect re-read covered two of five links in the latest pass
flags.detail: This session re-fetched link.amazon/B04G1MEwY (resolves to B0CDY277D3) and link.amazon/B0c8moW59 (resolves to B0DHZTCNR5). Both matched the register. The other three short links (P2, P3, P5) keep their 2026-11-19 reads and were not re-fetched in this pass.
flags.evidence_note: Submitted link for P2; the three unrefreshed short links are listed in data/p2/intent-links.json.
flags.how_to_resolve: Re-read all five short links in the next publishing pass. Not automated yet; a check that fails on a redirect change would close this gap.

flags.title: Session-8ff10f50 dimension values not re-confirmed in this pass
flags.detail: This session (arena/8ff10f50-prod2) could not re-read the official Amazon listings to confirm the product-table dimensions (D×W×H) and derived capacity-per-depth ratio for P1-P3 — the sandbox cannot reach amazon.com (egress is github.com, npm and PyPI only). Those values carry earlier read dates (2026-11-14) and are published with them, pending an owner re-read. Per the publication rule, values that cannot be confirmed from an official source at publishing time should be left blank and flagged rather than trusted by default; no value was inferred or filled in this pass.
flags.evidence_note: data/p2/products.json (dimensions_read 2026-11-14); data/p2/verification-2026-11-19.json (carried_prior_reads)
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner re-reads the three air-fryer listings and either re-confirms the dimensions (update read date) or blanks them and marks them unverified until confirmed.

flags.title: Disclosure strip rendered a double-paren label artifact — resolved 2026-11-19
flags.detail: Every published page rendered 'Product links on this site are paid links ((paid link)); …': the template wrapped the paid-link label in parentheses even though the label itself already contains them (data/p2/settings.json paid_link_label = '(paid link)'). Found in a line-by-line review of the built pages on 2026-11-19. Fixed at the generator (tools/build.py, DISCLOSURE_STRIP) so the wording cannot drift, and the new validity section of tools/checks.py fails the build if '((paid' ever appears again. The disclosure sentence, placement and footer repeat were unaffected.
flags.evidence_note: Built page as shipped on main at 3cd056a, line 146 (disclosure strip); review pass 2026-11-19, session arena/1ca951c0-prod2
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved 2026-11-19: generator fix + validity gate (tools/checks.py).

flags.title: products.html shipped duplicate id="P1..P5" — resolved 2026-11-19
flags.detail: The product cards and the fact-section headings both used id="P1" through id="P5", so five fragment anchors were ambiguous (invalid HTML; products.html#Pn resolves to the first occurrence in document order). Found in the 2026-11-19 review pass. Fact headings now anchor to facts-P1..P5; the cards keep P1..P5, so every existing products.html#Pn link (JSON-LD ItemList, buying guide, category pages, guides) still resolves to the same card it always did. Duplicate ids now fail the build (tools/checks.py validity).
flags.evidence_note: Built page as shipped on main at 3cd056a, line 232 (first duplicate); review pass 2026-11-19, session arena/1ca951c0-prod2
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved 2026-11-19: fact-heading anchors renamed + validity gate.

flags.title: DESIGN_PROMPT.md cites a different register lineage than the live site
flags.detail: The visual brief cites D-01/D-02 (brand 'The Crisp Counter', warm-editorial adoption), D-15 (mobile-first rules), Q-05 (photography path) and Q-10 (name clearance). Those ids belong to the predecessor Countercraft/Zone4 registers: in the live registers D-01 is the tagged-Special-Links decision, the photography question is Q-P05 with decision D-22 (now carried), name clearance is Q-19, and D-02/D-15 do not exist here. The brief's brand name also differs from the shipped wordmark ('Prod2', decision D-P03). A reader who follows the brief's ids from the live decision log lands on unrelated decisions. Publication is not blocked; the brief must be reconciled before the design pass implements it. Verified 2026-11-20: the live pages and tools/build.py both derive from data/p2/*.json and content/pages/*.html; DESIGN_PROMPT.md names the same lineage. Remaining discrepancy is prose only.
flags.evidence_note: Line-by-line cross-reference check 2026-11-19 (session arena/1ca951c0-prod2); brief ids compared against data/p2/*.json and data/imported/zone4/
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved 2026-11-20: DESIGN_PROMPT.md synced to the shipped stack (fonts, imagery, lineage).

flags.title: Google Search Console verification is not done (owner action)
flags.detail: The publication ships everything Search Console needs to be claimed and submitted (unique titles and meta descriptions, canonical URLs, sitemap.xml, robots.txt with the Sitemap line, RSS feed). Verification itself needs the owner's Google account: either the HTML-tag token (a slot exists in data/p2/settings.json -> search_console.verification_token, currently empty). Cross-reference: Q-P06 (owner domain control) and Q-P08 (who verifies). or the DNS/HTML-file method. Until then no search performance data exists, so topic selection stays editorial (Q-P02).
flags.evidence_note: Google Search Central: Search Console is the first-party source of search query data; verification requires the property owner.
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner verifies the property in Search Console (paste the meta token into settings.json and rebuild, or use the HTML-file method), then submits sitemap.xml and the feed. Prepared checklist: measurement.html. Cross-ref: Q-P08, SG-29.

flags.title: Reader-capture form ships disconnected (privacy basis open)
flags.detail: The 'What should we answer next?' form is live but sends nothing anywhere: the consent basis for collecting an email address (Q-47) is not settled, and no capture endpoint is configured (data/p2/settings.json -> reader_capture). A visitor's typed question stays in their own browser. This is deliberate: the mechanism is built, the gate in front of it is real.
flags.evidence_note: FTC guidance cited for the disclosure/consent standard that the capture consent text must meet (S07).
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner settles the consent text and the privacy-page wording (Q-47), then sets the capture endpoint URL in settings.json and rebuilds; the form activates with the consent checkbox required. Related: SG-30, SG-04.

flags.title: Disclosure wording did not match Operating Agreement section 5
flags.detail: The site published 'As an Amazon Associate we earn from qualifying purchases.' Section 5 prescribes the first-person form, and section 6(a) makes a violation of section 5 a material breach of the Agreement.
flags.evidence_note: Section 5, quoted verbatim in data/p2/verification-2026-11-20.json; page updated 2025-10-15; read 2026-11-20.
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved 2026-11-20: settings.disclosure_sentence and the release gate now use the prescribed first-person sentence on every page. Note that section 5 permits 'any substantially similar statement previously allowed', so the previous wording was arguably compliant; the prescribed form removes the doubt.

flags.title: A paid call to action labelled 'Compare all five' linked to a single product listing
flags.detail: The front-page CTA 'Compare all five' was an Amazon Associates link to P1's listing. The label promised a comparison and delivered one product. Program Policies 2(b) prohibits misleading claims, and a button label that does not describe its destination is the mildest form of that.
flags.evidence_note: Program Policies, updated 2026-04-14, section 2(b) misleading-claims sentence; read 2026-11-20.
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved 2026-11-20: the CTA now points at compare.html, and the gate's link check keeps sponsored links distinguishable from internal navigation.

flags.title: Carousel prices and ratings on a listing belong to neighbouring ASINs, not the product
flags.detail: On the 2026-11-20 reads, the visible price or star figure in several listings belonged to a different ASIN shown in the 'Customers who viewed this item also viewed' carousel. P1's page carried a star rating and count belonging to B0B7C327LK; P3's carried a price belonging to B0CNY1YVDD; P5's carried a price belonging to B0FXBQ3KX1. None of these is the target product's own value.
flags.evidence_note: Observed 2026-11-20 and recorded with the neighbouring ASIN identified in data/p2/verification-2026-11-20.json (finding V-03). The numeric values are held in that register only and are not republished on the site (F-02).
flags.how_to_resolve: Standing practice: any price or rating read from a listing must be tied to the ASIN in the canonical URL, never to a figure elsewhere on the page. This is one of the reasons the site publishes no prices or ratings at all.

flags.title: Prior verification records stated the sandbox could not reach Amazon, so figures were carried forward
flags.detail: The 2026-11-19 records state that egress was limited to code-hosting hosts and that listing values were taken from earlier dated records rather than re-read. On 2026-11-20 the listings and official policy pages were retrieved and read directly.
flags.evidence_note: All five listings plus the Operating Agreement and Program Policies were fetched on 2026-11-20; each value is recorded with the chunk it came from in data/p2/verification-2026-11-20.json.
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved 2026-11-20: the current pass is a direct read, not a carried-forward one. The carried-forward dates in data/p2/products.json remain accurate for the values they describe and are labelled as such.

flags.title: Archived builds are reachable on the live host and are only excluded by robots.txt
flags.detail: Archived builds (archive/counter-notes-v1, archive/counter-notes-docs, archive/counter-edit-build, 121 files) are reachable on the live host and are excluded only by a robots.txt rule. Same root cause as F-P20: Pages is in legacy root mode, so every archived directory is served. robots.txt stops well-behaved crawlers and nothing else. The 2026-11-20 workflow change publishes docs/ only going forward, but the archived trees remain readable until the owner switches the Pages source. 2026-11-20 extension (arena/37b265a4-prod2): .github/workflows/pages.yml builds and uploads docs/ only, but the Pages API still reports build_type legacy with source main / (read 2026-11-20). While that remains, the workflow’s docs-only rule does not control what is served; the repository root, data/ and archive/ stay public. This is the same mismatch recorded in F-P20; it is extended here, not duplicated.
flags.evidence_note: docs/ artifact is the only publish root (.github/workflows/pages.yml); gate section 'exposition' in tools/checks.py; Pages API showed build_type=legacy, source=main,/ on 2026-11-20.
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner flips Pages source to GitHub Actions (see F-P20). Archived builds can then be dropped or left in git, unserved.

flags.title: The whole working repository is readable on the live host (root-mode Pages)
flags.detail: GitHub Pages is in legacy mode with the source set to the repository ROOT: the Pages API returns build_type=legacy, source={branch: main, path: /}. Checked on 2026-11-20, https://…/Prod2/data/p2/settings.json returns the settings register as JSON to an anonymous reader. Counted at the same moment: data/ 42 files, content/ 27, tools/ 5, scripts/ 4, tests/ 1, archive/ 121 — 196 source files reachable by guessing a path. Nothing secret is in them (the tracking ID and disclosure text are published on purpose and the capture and analytics endpoints are empty), but it is not the intended surface, it exposes drafts and the archived builds, and robots.txt is a crawler convention, not access control. The token available to this session cannot change the setting: a PUT to build_type=workflow returns 403. Mitigated in-repo as far as a build can: the Pages workflow uploads the docs/ artifact only, and the new exposition gate section refuses any source directory inside docs/. If an owner ever flips the source to GitHub Actions, this whole class disappears. 2026-11-20 R-01 addition: the public copy of data/p2/settings.json on the live host (fetched through the fetch tool) shows brand.name “Prod2” and an earlier last_change, while the repository copy and the live index title show “The Crisp Counter”. The cause is not established (possibly a fetch-tool cache or a stale copy). Recorded here, not treated as conclusive.
flags.evidence_note: Anonymous GET of a source file on the live host, 2026-11-20; Pages API reports build_type=legacy, source=main,/; count from `python3 tools/root_mirror.py --report`.
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions (one setting). Then confirm /data/p2/settings.json and /tools/build.py return 404 and close F-P19/F-P20.

flags.title: Seven files cited an analytics endpoint path that does not exist — resolved 2026-11-20
flags.detail: measurement.html, privacy.html, events.json, questions.json, settings.json, suggestions.json, ENGINE.md and EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md all described the endpoint as 'analytics-endpoint/server.py'. No such file has ever been committed at any point in this repository's history. The only endpoint is server.mjs at the root. Every reference was corrected on 2026-11-20, flag F-19's evidence URL was repointed, and a gate rule now fails the build if a page cites a local path that does not exist.
flags.evidence_note: server.mjs committed at the repo root; ANALYTICS-ENDPOINT.md documents it; npm test exercises tests/server.test.mjs
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolved 2026-11-20: all references name server.mjs; gate rule added to tools/checks.py.

flags.title: The site's five events and the endpoint's accepted vocabulary do not match
flags.detail: measure.js would send page_view, outbound_click, guide_read_75, category_click and feed_click. server.mjs accepts page_view, outbound_click, guide_open, category_open, rss_feed_click, chooser_completed, article_half_read, disclosure_viewed, cta_click, product_click, filter_apply and guide_read. Three of the five site events (guide_read_75, category_click, feed_click) would be rejected by the only endpoint in this repository. Nothing is lost today because the endpoint is not hosted and the site transmits nothing, but connecting them unchanged would silently under-count. Not corrected in this pass because choosing the vocabulary is a decision, not a typo.
flags.evidence_note: the allowedEvents set in server.mjs vs the event list in docs/assets/js/measure.js and data/p2/events.json
flags.how_to_resolve: Pick one vocabulary: extend server.mjs to accept the three site events, or change measure.js to emit the endpoint's names. Record it as a decision, then gate the two lists against each other.
flags.resolution: Resolved 2026-11-20 (arena/644d217b-prod2). The collector now accepts the site's five documented events (page_view, outbound_click, guide_read_75, category_click, feed_click) and keys each one correctly: page_view reads the site's path field instead of collapsing to /unknown, outbound_click keeps the ASIN, category_click and guide_read_75 are aggregated rather than rejected. The preserved Countercraft event family is still accepted, so nothing that already posts to this endpoint is dropped. A regression test (tests/server.test.mjs) reads the event names out of assets/js/measure.js itself, and tools/checks.py section 'measurement' now FAILS the build when the client can send a name the endpoint rejects. Hosting the endpoint is still owner action (F-19/Q-23).

flags.title: Working brand “The Crisp Counter” adopted on the owner's directive without formal trademark clearance
flags.detail: The 2026-11-20 anti-slop pass replaced the repository codename 'Prod2' on reader-facing surfaces with the design brief's working brand (decision D-P18). A preliminary web search that day returned no conflicting kitchen-appliance brand in the first page of results, but no formal USPTO/state/common-law search has been run. Until clearance, the brand is provisional and one-line reversible (data/p2/settings.json).
flags.evidence_note: USPTO trademark search — the formal check that would resolve this; the preliminary 2026-11-20 web-search record sits in D-P10's sources.
flags.how_to_resolve: Run the formal clearance (Q-P10 / Q-19), then either ratify the name in the decision log or revert via settings.json and rebuild.

flags.title: Submitted link.amazon short links did not resolve to product listings in the 2026-11-20 live re-check
flags.detail: On 2026-11-20 the five submitted link.amazon URLs were fetched with redirects followed. Four resolved to the Amazon homepage (https://www.amazon.com/) and one returned HTTP 500. The five ASIN listing pages (https://www.amazon.com/dp/{ASIN}) were all live and their titles match data/p2/products.json exactly. The register's earlier redirect history (2026-11-14, 16, 17, 19) recorded these short links resolving to the same ASINs. The site does not publish the short links as buy paths (they render as quoted text under F-03), so no reader-facing link is broken by this. The difference is not explained: it may be a fetch-tool artifact or a change in the short-link service. Intended-ASIN fields were NOT changed. Full record: data/p2/live-check-2026-11-20-722181aa.json. Third read, arena/e292fb4d-prod2 (same day, fetch tool): all five resolved to https://www.amazon.com/ (homepage, title 'Amazon.com. Spend less. Smile more.'); no product page. Record: data/p2/live-check-2026-11-20-e292fb4d.json. Status stays open. Second observation, same day (arena/d5157db6-prod2, data/p2/live-check-2026-11-20-d5157db6.json): all five short links again resolved to https://www.amazon.com/ (the homepage); the link that returned HTTP 500 earlier today (B0f3GKalj, P5) now also resolves to the homepage. The problem is therefore not limited to one link and is not a one-off error. Still unresolved; still no reader-facing link is affected.
flags.evidence_note: Live /dp/ listing for P1 (title matches register). Short-link observations and the four other ASIN pages are in data/p2/live-check-2026-11-20-722181aa.json.
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner (or any reviewer with a normal browser) opens each of the five link.amazon URLs and records the final URL and ASIN in a dated redirect observation in data/p2/intent-links.json. If the short links no longer resolve to the registered ASINs, the intended_asin values stay as the /dp/ pages show and the mismatch is escalated under F-03 / F-57.

flags.title: “Check price on Amazon” button label on product cards needs a copy decision
flags.detail: Each product card on the shop front and shop page ends in a button labelled “Check price on Amazon”. No price is published on the site (F-02; decision D-P11). The label shows no price, so no violation is claimed. It is flagged for review because Program Policies §2(b) (read 2026-11-20) restricts what a site may show about prices, and the owner should confirm that a call to action that refers to price is acceptable. Alternative wording, such as “View on Amazon”, is a copy decision for the owner and is not made here.
flags.evidence_note: S-POL §2(b), read 2026-11-20 (policy page chunk 3). The button text is generated in tools/build.py.
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner chooses the button wording. A change is a one-line edit in tools/build.py followed by a rebuild and the release gate. Nothing changes until the owner decides.

flags.title: The repository executive summary published a listed-price column, which the site withholds
flags.detail: EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md (served publicly at the live host because Pages is in legacy root mode) carried a “Price (as listed)” column with five dollar figures from the 2026-11-19 pass. The register withholds prices (F-02; D-P11; Program Policies §2(b), read 2026-11-20). Earlier records (F-P17; data/p2/verification-2026-11-20.json V-03) state that carousel prices on these listings belong to neighbouring ASINs. This session did not re-read the carousels, so whether any of the five figures came from a neighbouring product is not verified here. The column has been replaced with “withheld”. No figure was corrected, because no price is published.
flags.evidence_note: Live file as served 2026-11-20 (fetch tool). Neighbouring-price mechanism: F-P17; carousel observations in data/p2/verification-2026-11-19.json and data/p2/verification-2026-11-20.json. Policy: S-POL §2(b), read 2026-11-20.
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner decides whether any price policy changes (suggestion SG-05 covers a dated-snapshot option). Until then the column stays withheld. Owner also decides whether the root-mode exposure of EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md and other repository files is fixed (F-P19, F-P20).

flags.title: Two same-day fetch-tool reads of the owner short links disagree for two of five links, so the outcome is not reproducible
flags.detail: F-P24 (arena/722181aa-prod2, 2026-11-20) and an independent same-day re-read in arena/37b265a4-prod2 (data/p2/verification-2026-11-20.json, key r01_reread_2026_11_20) disagree on two of the five short links. link.amazon/B02NbDxp3: the R-01 read reached the intended listing (B09B7SB46R); the other read reached the Amazon homepage. link.amazon/B0f3GKalj: the R-01 read reached the Amazon homepage; the other read recorded HTTP 500. The other three links read the same way in both: link.amazon/B04G1MEwY and link.amazon/B0c8moW59 reached the homepage, and link.amazon/B00hJ57DV reached the homepage. Two same-day fetch-tool reads are not reproducible, so neither is taken as the answer. The outcome is decided only by the logged-out browser check in Q-P18.
flags.evidence_note: R-01 re-read: data/p2/verification-2026-11-20.json (r01_reread_2026_11_20). Other read: data/p2/live-check-2026-11-20-722181aa.json (arena/722181aa-prod2). Redirect history: data/p2/intent-links.json.
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner checks each link in a logged-out private window and in the Associates-enrolled browser and records the final URL (Q-P18). Until then the register keeps both reads as dated history and claims neither outcome.

flags.title: products.json and the intent record describe the short links as resolving to their listings; the 2026-11-20 reads do not confirm this for every link
flags.detail: products.json (short_link field on each product) and data/p2/intent-links.json (intent record and the 2026-11-19 redirect history) still describe the owner short links as resolving to the registered ASINs, and no status for the 2026-11-20 reads has been added to products.json. The 2026-11-20 reads (F-P24, F-P27) confirmed one of five links at its intended ASIN in the R-01 read. Intent fields (intended_asin, official_listing_url) and observed redirect targets are kept in separate fields and are not merged. The 2026-11-20 observations are dated history beside the 2026-11-19 record. Nothing in those files is overwritten by this flag, and no intent field is changed.
flags.evidence_note: data/p2/products.json short_link fields; data/p2/intent-links.json observed_redirect_history (2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20 entries); data/p2/verification-2026-11-20.json r01_reread_2026_11_20.
flags.how_to_resolve: Owner completes the logged-out browser check (Q-P18). After that the owner decides whether products.json keeps the short_link field as recorded, and whether intent-links.json gets a dated status note. No intent field is changed until then.

flags.title: All 30 published pages shipped a stylesheet containing git conflict markers (fixed and gated in this pass)
flags.detail: On 2026-11-20 the file every page loads, assets/css/site.css, began with '<<<<<<< HEAD', '=======' and '>>>>>>> origin/main' at lines 1, 48 and 75. Both sides of that merge had also lost a closing brace, so two @font-face blocks ran together and the HEAD block was missing its terminator. Every workflow was green, tools/checks.py reported ALL CHECKS PASSED, and the site deployed in that state. Root cause of the miss: no check read the stylesheet for structure, and no session in this repository has ever rendered a page - measured this pass, the Python and Node browser toolkits install but the Chrome-for-Testing binary and the Debian font packages do not download. A strict CSS parser discards an unclosed block, so the tail of the design system was at risk of silently not applying. Note the interaction with F-P25: the defect was first noticed through a conflict-marker check, but a marker check alone does not catch a silently unclosed block, which is why this row is separate. Verified after repair: 245 top-level rules parse with 0 errors (before the merge of the briefs pass), braces balance, and the final @media print rule is fully consumed. This branch keeps both complete font stacks (six static latin subsets plus three variable faces) rather than choosing between them, because each is a valid fallback for the other. The condition that caused the miss is now gated by tools/design_qa.py (/tools/design_qa.py in this repo), which fails the build on markers, on an unclosed block, on a dangling var() token, on a missing or invalid font file, and on a body that paints no background or text colour.
flags.evidence_note: The stylesheet readers are served. Confirm line 1 is a comment rather than a conflict marker, then run python3 tools/design_qa.py in a checkout to reproduce the gate.
flags.how_to_resolve: No owner action required: repaired and gated in this pass. For review, open the live stylesheet and confirm line 1 is a comment, then run the gate.

flags.title: The publishing cadence could not be audited: nothing linked a publish to the schedule
flags.detail: data/p2/calendar.json declares 'one new question-shaped guide' every 14 days, and the nine queue slots are spaced exactly 14 days apart (measured: the only distinct gap between consecutive slots is 14 days; first_publish 2026-11-19 + 14 = next_due 2026-12-03). What did not exist was any machine-checkable link between a page that actually shipped and that schedule. Six reader pages published 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20 — including today's two guides and one long read — left next_due_utc untouched at 2026-12-03, so the front page could keep saying 'a new guide every two weeks' whether or not the register kept score. A second inconsistency came with it: queue slot 1 promises to answer 'Preheat, shake, or don't' from 'manual-ritual features verified on the three listings', but a listing states a feature, not a ritual — that slot is now marked blocked on Q-P19 instead of scheduled.
flags.evidence_note: Gaps and dates computed from data/p2/calendar.json on 2026-11-20 by tools/checks.py's cadence section, not typed in by hand.
flags.how_to_resolve: Closed by the gate rule; the remaining decision — whether a 14-day rhythm is actually resourced — is Q-P20.
flags.resolution: Fixed 2026-11-20 with a rule rather than a cleanup: the publish gate (tools/checks.py, section 'cadence') now fails the build when the newest recorded publish + the declared interval falls after next_due_utc, so shipping silently without advancing the schedule is impossible. next_due_utc advanced to 2026-12-04, publishes are dated in calendar.published_early, and slot 1 carries blocked_by: Q-P19 with a status the guides hub renders.

flags.title: Two archived builds are still reachable by path while Pages serves the repository root
flags.detail: site/ (the archived Countercraft build, 25 tracked files) and archive/countertop-dispatch/ both sit in the tree. While the Pages source is the repo root (F-P19), each is fetchable by URL, and neither carries a canonical pointing at this site: site/index.html is titled 'Countercraft — Kitchen gear worth the counter space.' A search engine that reaches either sees a second brand, a second copy of the same guide set and no signal about which one is the site. No price or rating was found in those files by this pass (grep for a $-then-digits pattern returned nothing), so this is an indexing and brand-dilution exposure, not a disclosure one.
flags.evidence_note: git ls-files site → 25 files, read 2026-11-20; robots.txt previously disallowed only /Prod2/archive/.
flags.how_to_resolve: One of two owner-side moves: set Settings → Pages → Source to 'GitHub Actions' so only the docs/ artifact is served (F-P19, which removes the exposure entirely), or approve deleting site/ and archive/ from the published branch. Interim mitigation shipped 2026-11-20: the generated robots.txt now disallows /Prod2/site/ as well as /Prod2/archive/. A robots line is a request, not a control — the source change is the fix.

flags.title: A cited source contradicts itself on a unit conversion (eggs: 160°F printed as 73.9°C)
flags.detail: The Nebraska Extension air-fryer handout's temperature table prints 'Eggs | 160°F (73.9°C)'. 160°F is 71.1°C, which is what the USDA FSIS chart prints in the same position; 73.9°C is 165°F. The two pages agree on the Fahrenheit figure this site publishes, and the extension table also omits the FSIS chart's 'Leftovers' row entirely (165°F). Nothing on this site converts or repairs a source: we publish the FSIS figure with its read date and leave the discrepancy visible here, because 'fixing' a citation silently is how a register becomes fiction.
flags.evidence_note: Read 2026-11-20 alongside https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart (page dated Apr 14, 2025). Both fetches are recorded in data/p2/verification-2026-11-20-e1dbef32.json.
flags.how_to_resolve: No action for this site. It closes if the source corrects its table; a reviewer comparing our numbers against the extension page should expect the Celsius column to differ on that one row.

flags.title: The design brief promised FAQPage structured data that the generator never emitted
flags.detail: DESIGN_PROMPT.md, under 'Organic traffic hooks', states that every guide page is built for search with 'FAQPage + Article structured data'. tools/build.py's jsonld_for() emitted WebSite, BreadcrumbList, ItemList and Article — and no FAQPage anywhere. No reader-facing page claims FAQ rich results, so no reader was misled, but the brief a future rebuild is supposed to implement was describing markup that did not exist, which is the same defect class as F-P12 (documentation asserting a shipped state the code does not have).
flags.evidence_note: jsonld_for() as merged at 51a02ac: no FAQPage node; the brief's line is at DESIGN_PROMPT.md 'Organic traffic hooks'.
flags.how_to_resolve: Emit the markup, or correct the brief — and decide which, on evidence rather than by habit.
flags.resolution: Both, 2026-11-20. The generator now derives FAQPage from the rendered page: where a page shows two or more visible question-and-answer blocks, the same list becomes mainEntity, so markup cannot describe content a reader cannot see. DESIGN_PROMPT.md was rewritten to say what ships and why the search benefit is limited: Google's 2023 announcement restricted FAQ rich results to well-known authoritative government and health sites ('For all other sites, this rich result will no longer be shown regularly'), its changelog records 'Removing documentation for the FAQ rich result feature' in June 2026, and its supported-features gallery as read 2026-11-20 does not list FAQ. The markup is therefore descriptive, not a rich-results tactic, and the site says so instead of implying a SERP promise.

flags.title: Structured data published placeholder facts: gtin13 null and a brand named 'unknown'
flags.detail: The ItemList/Product nodes built for index, compare and products hard-coded "gtin13": null and filled a missing brand with the literal string 'unknown'. A null identifier is noise a crawler parses; a brand called 'unknown' is worse — it is an invented value inside machine-readable data, in a project whose whole rule is that an unread value stays blank. Today the placeholder never fires, because all five products do have a listed brand (Chefman, Emeril, Chefman, ThermoMaven, CHEF iQ); the defect is latent, and would have appeared the first time a listing read returned no brand.
flags.evidence_note: jsonld_for() at 51a02ac: "brand": {"@type": "Brand", "name": p.get("brand") or "unknown"}.
flags.how_to_resolve: Omit a property when the register has no value for it; never fill a field with a placeholder.
flags.resolution: Fixed 2026-11-20 at the generator: the Product node now carries only fields the register actually holds (name, sku, category, url, description, and brand only when a brand was read), and the null gtin13 is gone. The evidence rule now covers the JSON-LD graph, not just the visible page.

flags.title: The guides hub published an orphaned sentence, and no gate could see it
flags.detail:
content/pages/guides.html closed its lede with

and then continued the same sentence outside the paragraph, ending in a second stray

. A reader saw a fragment stranded between blocks; the built page carried an unmatched end tag. The gate checked nested

and duplicate ids but never counted paragraph balance, so the defect was invisible to the machine that publishes the site.
flags.evidence_note: The file as merged at 51a02ac — the lede's second sentence sits after the closing tag.
flags.how_to_resolve: Fixed 2026-11-20 in the same pass that found it: the fragment now opens one paragraph and closes it once.
flags.resolution:
The sentence is back inside the lede, and tools/checks.py's validity section now counts

openings against

closings on every built page, so this class fails the build instead of shipping. Reproduced before the fix (the gate printed the exact mismatch), then fixed at the fragment.

flags.title: Two pages shipped FAQPage markup that did not match the page a reader sees
flags.detail: Found while wiring the guide FAQ blocks against the new faq gate, and reproduced on origin/main (551c633c) in a clean worktree. decide.html carried a four-question FAQPage node with no question-and-answer content visible anywhere on the page — the strings appear only inside the JSON-LD script — while index.html showed six visible FAQ items and described four of them in the markup, with every answer paraphrased rather than mirrored. Both nodes were hand-written copies of a list the page already had, in the same file, one function apart: exactly the duplication that made the landing copy drift. Google's FAQ guidance requires the marked-up content to be the content shown, so this is a compliance-shaped defect, not a tidiness one.
flags.evidence_note: jsonld_for() on main: the index and decide branches each restate the FAQ by hand; hook_landing_faq() renders six. Reproduce with `git worktree add /tmp/m origin/main && cd /tmp/m && python3 tools/build.py && grep -c faq-item docs/decide.html` (returns 0).
flags.how_to_resolve: Make the structured data impossible to write twice.
flags.resolution: Fixed 2026-11-20 in the generator rather than in the copy: both pages' FAQ blocks now render from one list (LANDING_FAQ, DECIDE_FAQ) and the FAQPage node is derived from the rendered content by faq_pairs(), with tags stripped so the machine answer is the reader's answer word for word. decide.html gained a visible four-question block; index.html's node now covers all six. tools/checks.py's faq section enforces the pairing on every page, so a markup-only FAQ fails the build (D-P26).

flags.title: origin/main shipped red: the per-page script broke the site's own one-site gate
flags.detail: At the merged tip of main (551c633, after PRs #58-#60) `python3 tools/build.py && python3 tools/checks.py` fails two sections: one-site reports that decide.html's page script carries no ?v= cache-buster, and a11y reports a heading-level skip in suggestions.html (the review banner jumps h1 to h3). Verified by building and gating origin/main in a clean worktree, not inferred from the log. The Pages workflow runs the same gate, so the merge should not have been possible on a workflow-gated deploy; the site publishes from the committed docs/ artifact, which is why a red gate was survivable at all.
flags.evidence_note: Reproduce: `git worktree add /tmp/m origin/main && cd /tmp/m && python3 tools/build.py && python3 tools/checks.py | tail -5`.
flags.how_to_resolve: Fix both, and stop trusting a green merge that was never gated.
flags.resolution: Fixed 2026-11-20 in this integration: build_page now appends ?v={ASSET_V} to per-page scripts the way LAYOUT does for site.js and measure.js, and the suggestions.html banner heading was promoted to h2 (styled by a new .callout h2 rule so it still reads as a callout). Both sections pass on this branch.

flags.title: The gate that claims to parse the stylesheet parsed nothing, because of a query string
flags.detail: The assets section collects asset URLs from built pages and keeps the ones ending .css or .js. Every real link carries the ?v= cache-buster the one-site section requires, so the stylesheet — the file whose corruption broke all 30 pages on 2026-11-20 (F-P29) — never entered the loop. The section was not empty and so never complained, because one script (decide.js, unversioned per F-P37) matched by accident. Net effect: 'no conflict markers, tokens defined, every class used by a page exists' was asserted against a single JavaScript file and reported as covering the design system.
flags.evidence_note: The linked-URL filter `rel.endswith((".css", ".js"))` before the ?v= suffix is stripped. Reproduce by printing css_files with and without the fix.
flags.how_to_resolve: Resolve the URL to a path before matching it.
flags.resolution: Fixed 2026-11-20: the assets section now strips the query string before matching and existence-testing, so docs/assets/css/site.css is genuinely parsed on every build — which is also what made the F-P37 fix safe to land (the version suffix no longer hides the file). With the stylesheet actually in scope, every class the 36 built pages use must exist in it, which is the assertion F-P29 was written for.

flags.title: README documented 14 gate sections while the gate ran 21
flags.detail: Both the quick-start line and the status table on main read '14 sections'; tools/checks.py at the same commit runs 21 (pages, disclosure, links, validity, facts, claims, derived, chrome, seo, publication, a11y, structured, assets, longreads, shop, exposition, measurement, briefs, one-site, integrity, freshness). Seven sections were added without touching the document a new session reads first — the same failure mode as F-P12 and F-P32: the code moved, the prose about the code stayed. It matters here because COORDINATION.md tells every session to run the gate and trust it.
flags.evidence_note: grep -n 'sections' README.md on main; count with `grep -cE '^\s+check\("' tools/checks.py`.
flags.how_to_resolve: State the count once, or do not state it at all.
flags.resolution: README and ENGINE now read 23 (21 + this pass's faq and cadence), and the section table lists each one. A future-proof alternative — generating the sentence from checks.py — is recorded as SG-50 territory rather than done here, since the copy lives in two documents.
